goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — The light/dark color values are reversed; use $primary, 70% for light themes and $secondary, 30% for dark themes

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for mobile/modal.scss line 102, the change is from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The finding claims the values are reversed. Examining the pattern used throughout the rest of the diff, the consistent pattern is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: X%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 100-X%))` - for example, 50%/50%, 70%/30%, 40%/60%, etc. The original value was 70% lightness on $primary. Following the pattern, it should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`, but the diff shows 30%/70% which is indeed reversed compared to the established pattern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — The h3 light-theme color changes from $primary, 20% to 50%, substantially reducing contrast; use $primary, 20% / $secondary, 80%

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in mobile/topic-post.scss line 182, the h3 color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This means the light-theme value changed from 20% lightness to 50% lightness, which is a significant contrast reduction. The finding suggests using 20%/80% to maintain the original contrast, which is a valid concern about accessibility/readability.
